notes: B2 VETO FEEDBACK: the model is told what the gate will refuse, and which proposal was vetoed. BUILT 2026-09-11 AND NEVER DEPLOYED -- 15 days. It is the agreed next step after three cooldown canaries (38bebdd/placebo-b, bb1af53/isolated-a, bb1af53/board-a) all read REVERT and established that the WAIT is not the bottleneck: a shorter cooldown bought +41% model calls that became vetoed re-proposals of just-failed actions (board-a: vetoed re-proposals 13.9 -> 35.6/bot-h, executed decisions control-adjusted -2%). The prompt said `rejected: cooldown (gather with these args failed recently)` -- not WHICH args, not what else is off-limits -- and the 7B re-proposed it. TWO HALVES, AIMED AT THE TWO BIGGEST VETO CLASSES. Measured 2026-09-26 over 12 sampled bots / 18 bot-h / 536 veto lines: repeat_loop 275 (51.3%), cooldown 124 (23.1%), learned_avoid 72 (13.4%), deposit_not_worth_it 37, bad_args 16. (1) prompt.mjs gains offLimitsLine() -- the unexpired failed-cooldown entries, longest first, capped at 6 entries and 240 chars, EMPTY when nothing is off-limits so an idle bot's prompt does not grow: that attacks `cooldown`. (2) cognitive.mjs's lastOutcome names the vetoed proposal with its args (`rejected gather block=oak_log: cooldown (...)`) where it said `rejected: cooldown`: that attacks `repeat_loop`, which IS the re-proposal loop. 74.4% of vetoes between them. EXPOSURE IS NOT THE RISK HERE, unlike blindstep-02 (aborted at +58 min with zero exposure after board-c collapsed from 25.6 refusal-rows/bot-h to 0.56 boxed episodes/bot-h in 24 h). The gate writes a 45 s cooldown on every skill failure (FAILED_COOLDOWN_MS unset in all 80 env files, so config.mjs's 45000 applies) and the fleet fails ~81 skill attempts/bot-h, so 81 x 45 s = 3,645 s of coverage per 3,600 s hour: the table is non-empty essentially always. That is an INFERENCE from a measured quantity, which is why the floor below is 9% of the point estimate rather than 40%. WHY THERE IS AN INSTRUMENT IN THIS DIFF. There is NO veto event kind in the skill JSONL -- the rejection is log('warn','decision rejected') and reaches journald only. Verified: 116 distinct kinds over a 180-min fleet walk and the only veto-ish one is _veto_faces, which is gather target safety. So the primary endpoint is scraped from journald, and a single new row (`veto_feedback`) proves the change is LIVE AND EXERCISED rather than merely deployed. It measures the RENDERED line, not the table the gate holds, because offLimitsLine caps at 240 chars -- logging offLimits.length would be logging an intention, the defect that let blindstep-01 meet its exposure floor with no bot moving. A new EVENT and never a new field: the decision index is dynamic:strict and one unmapped key rejects the WHOLE document, which cost 8 days and ~1.4M absent decisions once already. THE INSTRUMENT IS PART OF MAKING B2 READABLE, NOT A SECOND EXPERIMENT -- it cannot change behaviour. Branch veto-b2-01 = efa2853 + cherry-pick 7d4f416 65c9090 + the instrument. Both cherry-picks auto-merged with no conflict. Diffing the original veto-feedback branch would have REVERTED 15 days of cognitive.mjs work: that branch is BEHIND main on that file (-187 lines), which is why this is a cherry-pick onto the deployed baseline and not a merge.

require.name: failed skill attempts (what writes a cooldown entry)

draw_exposure.note: The population this change targets is bots that GET VETOED, and the gate's cooldown map is written by skill FAILURES. Those are universal -- 26,054 failed skill rows in a 4 h fleet-wide window -- so exposure is not a binding constraint and this requirement is a tripwire against a pool that has gone quiet, not a filter. Stated explicitly rather than omitted: a draw_exposure block written for a different mechanism is blind to this one.

exposure.note: MEASURED, not inferred (see amendments): 10.9 rows/bot-h at steady state over 3.29 canary bot-h, so 10 bots x 180 min = 30 bot-h gives ~327 rows. 150 is 46% of that point estimate. It counts the gate SPEAKING -- a row only exists when the rendered off-limits line is non-empty -- so it cannot be met by a bot that merely ran. The first draft said 500 on an 8x-too-high inference and would have failed a working canary.

own_lines.note: _veto_feedback is UNEMITTABLE on efa2853: git grep for veto_feedback in efa2853 -- bots/src returns nothing, with a positive control on the identical query (kind: 'affordance_scan' -> 1 hit). Verified on the fleet over a 180-min walk, 113,773 rows / 80 bots / 116 distinct kinds: _veto_feedback = 0, positive controls on the SAME walk _affordance_scan 21,956, _veto_faces 1,104, _livelock_escape 567. A control-arm row means the arms are not what this read thinks they are. evidence=defect: a presence test against a structurally impossible value, not a statistical claim.

OFF_LIMITS_LINE_MAX = 240 is the bound that keeps this change from growing the prompt with the failure count. chars is measured on the RENDERED line, so a row over 240 means the cap is not holding in the field and the prompt is unbounded. Structurally impossible if the code is what the tests say it is; a defect if it happens.

primary.note: All vetoes per bot-hour, DiD, canary vs control, from journald, computed on the WARM window (post-deploy minute 30 onward) because the deploy restarts only the canary pool and the restart clears the very gate state this endpoint measures -- see amendments. GATE: KEEP needs vetoes_did_warm <= -5.03, the 5% one-sided bound of an EXHAUSTIVE same-shape null on identical code (C(12,2)=66, mean 0.00, sd 3.31), AND a component beating its own stratum centre: repeat_loop_did_warm <= +1.40 OR cooldown_did_warm <= -2.29 (hive-only range endpoints, n=6, NOT percentiles). REVERT needs vetoes_did_warm >= +5.17. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. learned_avoid_did_warm is a VALIDITY CHECK, not an endpoint: B2 cannot touch the lessons store, so a large value there means the aggregate is being driven by something other than the treatment. ONLY +180 AND +240 DECIDE (+180 gives ~25 warm canary bot-h; +40 gave 1.1 and is worthless). verdict.py puts `primary` in _ADVISORY (verdict.py:906) so THE GATE NEVER TESTS THIS -- a verdict.py KEEP means exposure, linkage and the death gate were clean and nothing more. The effect call is mine and is reported separately.
primary.gate_does_not_enforce_this: SOURCE-VERIFIED: verdict.py:906 lists `primary` in _ADVISORY, so the gate NEVER evaluates the effect. Positive controls in the same file: own_lines 4 hits, exposure 25 hits, both handled. The gate prints this itself -- falls-02's +180 verdict line names `primary` among 'NOT evaluated by this gate'. CONSEQUENCE: verdict.py will return KEEP for this run if the exposure floor is met, the two linkage lines hold and no two deaths land -- REGARDLESS of whether vetoes moved. That verdict is 'nothing objected', not 'it worked'. THE EFFECT CALL IS MINE, made at +180 against the gate below and the measured null, and it must be reported separately from verdict.py's verdict. Pre-registering the number here is still what stops it being chosen after the fact.

watch.note: REPORTED, NOT DECIDING. The share of decisions holding the full 6 entries. If that is high the cap is binding and the model is being shown a truncated view of what is off-limits -- a design question this canary is the only way to answer, and the reason `held` and `chars` are logged separately.

REPORTED. decisions/bot-h is the only endpoint with a tight MDE (~17%). B2 should not move it -- it changes prompt CONTENT, not cadence -- so a large move either way is a signal that something other than the intended mechanism is acting, most likely prompt length.

VOLUME, for the promotion decision and not for this verdict. ~1 row per decision means ~175k rows/day fleet-wide at 80 bots, roughly 44 MB/day raw against ~903 MB/day total -- about 5%. Acceptable for a 3 h canary; if this is promoted the emission should first be narrowed to fire on CHANGE of the entry set rather than every decision.

REPORTED at +30 and +90. Their noise band is wider than the +180 band and was not measured, so a crossing there means nothing -- the exact error that made a +90 crossing meaningless on 2026-09-23. Series required so a single crossing cannot decide.

ANSWERED ALREADY, at +25 min, and the answer is 0.0: held == 1 on 41 of 41 rows. The 6-entry cap never binds because a 45 s cooldown against a 30 s decision cadence can only ever hold the last failure. THE FOLLOW-UP THIS IMPLIES: for an off-limits line to carry information the model does not already have, it must be sourced from something with a longer memory than a 45 s cooldown -- the learned_avoid store is the obvious candidate, since it holds persistent cross-run counts (gather:{block:oak_log} at fails=2658, shared across all five hive-a bots) and learned_avoid is 13.4% of vetoes. That is a separate change and must not be bundled into this one.

mechanism_check.note: Same field as the exposure floor, deliberately: this change has one mechanism -- the model being shown the off-limits line. No row, no mechanism, and no other line can rescue it. Guards the canary-can-ship-inert failure (owner-01 ran 97 min as the baseline).

safety.floor: TWO canary deaths AND > 1.25x the control rate
safety.note: OWNER DECISION 2026-09-11, and gatecal measured it at 4.8% false-trip against a nominal 5% with 100% detection at 10x. This change cannot plausibly kill a bot -- it adds text to a prompt and emits a log row -- so a trip here would almost certainly be an unrelated death, which is exactly the case the two-death floor and the 1.25x ratio exist to absorb. One death is named in the read and is not a verdict.

pool_draw: DRAWN AT DEPLOY TIME by drawrec.sh with this run_id: ['board-a','hive-a','hive-c'] = 3 pools / 15 bots, rule v5 band widened to +-40% (stated by the draw), all-pool median 16.6 items/bot-h, 12h ledger exclusions removed board-c, hive-d, placebo-b, placebo-d. The draw offered 3 of a 4-pool target because the band had no more, and the read must say so: 15 bots, not 20. NOT the argmax -- board-a 13.1 and hive-a 14.9 sit BELOW the 16.6 median and hive-c is at it, so this draw does not build in regression to the mean. COVARIATE TO RECORD: all three drawn pools are on the 5080 half (half mix on offer was 5080:3, 3090:0), so the control arm carries every 3090 bot. That is a level difference the DiD absorbs, and inference-is-not-the-constraint measured the decision rate as identical across a 1.9x endpoint latency gap (91.10 vs 91.85), so it is recorded rather than treated as a confound. board-a additionally contains a trapped bot.
teardown: THREE steps: drop-ins, clearing canary_pool, AND restarting the pool's bots staggered 12 s apart, then confirm exactly two versions live. Then restore the golden analysis lib from ~/mcai-analysis/lib/ -- a deploy by any path other than ~/bin/fleet-deploy does not restore it, which is how the efa2853 promotion reverted telemetry.py and openloop.py.
known_residuals: RESTART ASYMMETRY, pre-registered rather than discovered. The deploy restarted ONLY the canary pool (hive-a, hive-c, 12 s stagger, 06:03-06:05Z). Control was not restarted. So the canary's POST window opens with a restart recovery while its PRE window is undisturbed and control has neither -- an asymmetry the DiD does NOT absorb, because it sits in the canary's own post-minus-pre term. It biases the canary's post rate DOWNWARD, i.e. toward a spurious KEEP on a 'fewer vetoes' endpoint. MAGNITUDE: decisions resume ~30 s after a bot reconnects, so the depressed period is a few minutes -- roughly 10-15% of the +30 window, ~5% of +90, and ~3% of +180. THAT IS A SECOND INDEPENDENT REASON ONLY +180 AND +240 DECIDE. Directly observed tonight: a 15-min sample right after the restart read 2.8 instrument rows/bot-h against a 10.9 steady state, a 3.9x transient. THE NULL DOES NOT COVER IT: both arms were undisturbed when the null was measured, so the null understates the noise for a restarted arm and the -5.03 bound is optimistic by an unmeasured amount. The project's own standard is 'identical restart treatment' (decision-cadence-event-driven), which this loop does not provide -- it restarts the canary pool only. Every canary on file carries this, and naming it is the honest alternative to pretending the DiD handles it.
HIVE-ONLY TREATMENT ARM, n=6 same-shape hive pairs. The component bounds derived from that subset are RANGE ENDPOINTS, not percentiles. Six is not a distribution and the read must not call them one.

licence.note: THE STRONGEST CLASS, and earned rather than asserted: efa2853 contains no logEvent with kind 'veto_feedback' (git grep empty; positive control kind: 'affordance_scan' -> 1 hit on the identical query), and a 180-min fleet walk of 113,773 rows over 116 distinct kinds found _veto_feedback = 0 with three positive controls on the same walk. Baseline silence is therefore structural, not statistical.

null_calibration.method: Both arms on IDENTICAL code (the live single-version fleet, efa2853+c7b045). journald scraped once over 6 h (16,663 veto lines, 85 units, 231,654 JSONL rows / 80 bots), then EVERY same-shape assignment enumerated: C(12,3)=220 exhaustively -- 3 pools of 5 from the 12 eligible pools, which is the shape drawrec ACTUALLY offered for this run (it drew 3 of a 4-pool target; the band had no more). Pre/post split at the midpoint, so the null matches the +180 read exactly (180 min pre, 180 min post). A 4-pool null over 400 of C(12,4)=495 gives p5 -5.03 / sd 3.09, essentially identical, so the band is robust to the pool count -- but the 3-pool numbers below are the ones that match this draw and are the ones that decide.
null_calibration.note: THIS IS WHY THE GATE IS NOT ZERO. The first draft said `KEEP if the DiD is negative`. A dry run with both arms on identical code returned vetoes_did = -5.27 and decisions_did = -5.44, which that rule would have KEPT -- the canary-gate-was-noise defect (leaf-01's typed -0.5 line tripping on nothing). The estimator is UNBIASED (mean 0.00, median -0.02 across all 220 assignments), so the problem is spread, not bias: sd 2.89 against a base rate of ~38 vetoes/bot-h. That -5.27 dry run sat at roughly the 5th percentile of its own null -- indistinguishable from nothing. POWER: the B2 design memo pre-registered >= 30% down control-adjusted, which at 29.8-38 vetoes/bot-h is a DiD of -9 to -11.4 -- 1.8x to 2.3x the 5% bound and beyond the MINIMUM of all 220 null assignments (-8.05). The registered target is detectable; a -5 result is not.

amendments.what: component gates re-centred on the drawn STRATUM; primary gate unchanged in substance
amendments.why: The draw came back hive-a + hive-c -- 2 pools / 10 bots, not the 3 pools / 15 bots offered six minutes earlier -- so the null was re-measured at the actual shape: C(12,2)=66, EXHAUSTIVE, on data ending STRICTLY AT THE DEPLOY INSTANT 2026-09-26T06:02:47Z, 16,614 pre-deploy veto lines. No canary data existed when this was computed and none was consulted; this corrects a MIS-SPECIFIED NULL, it does not respond to a result. THE FINDING THAT FORCED IT: the component nulls are STRATUM-DEPENDENT, and hive is the heaviest veto stratum (109-185 learned_avoid per 1k decisions against 3-16 elsewhere). Under the null, hive-only pairs centre at repeat_loop_did MEAN +3.01 (range +1.40..+4.63) while no-hive pairs centre at -1.51; and at cooldown_did MEAN -1.27 (range -2.29..-0.25) against no-hive +0.64. So the pooled gates would have BOTH blocked a true KEEP (requiring repeat_loop <= -6.18 when this stratum's null floor is +1.40) AND licensed a false one (cooldown <= -2.05 when this stratum's null reaches -2.29 on its own). For the PRIMARY the hive-only null is unbiased and tighter (mean +0.01, median +0.01, range -4.58..+4.59), so the pooled p5 -5.03 is kept as the conservative choice. HONEST LIMIT: n=6 hive-only assignments. A '5th percentile' of six numbers is the minimum, so these component bounds are RANGE ENDPOINTS, not percentiles, and they are used as direction-plus-magnitude checks rather than as tests. Stated because six is not a distribution.

amendments.what: exposure floor 500 -> 150. My arithmetic was wrong by 8x and the instrument found it at +25 min.
amendments.why: I registered 500 on the claim that the off-limits table is 'non-empty essentially always', inferred from 81 failed skill attempts/bot-h x a 45 s cooldown = 3,645 s of coverage per 3,600 s hour, so ~91 rows/bot-h. MEASURED at steady state over 25 min / 3.29 canary bot-h: 10.9 rows/bot-h, which gives ~327 rows over 10 bots x 3 h -- BELOW a floor of 500. The floor would have failed on a canary whose mechanism is demonstrably live, closing it INCONCLUSIVE on my arithmetic: the drop5-01 failure in a new costume. 150 is 46% of the measured point estimate, the same conservatism falls-02 used. A first 15-min sample read 2.8 rows/bot-h and I did NOT amend on it, because failedCooldowns starts empty on restart and the pool had just been restarted on a 12 s stagger -- that was a restart transient and believing it would have been believing a cheap negative. WHY THE RATE IS 10.9 AND NOT 91, which is the real finding: across 41 rows `held` is ALWAYS EXACTLY 1 and `secs_max` is ALWAYS EXACTLY 15, while `chars` (111-136) and `skills` (gather 33, goto/surface/mine/explore 2 each) vary -- so the instrument is reading real varying data and the invariants are structural. decisionCooldownMs = 30000 (env, all 80 bots) spaces decisions exactly 30 s apart and failedCooldownMs = 45000 (config default, unset in every env file) gives a cooldown a 45 s life. 45 - 30 = 15, every time. So the table can hold only the skill just failed, with 15 s left, and the max=6 entry cap and the 240-char bound CAN NEVER BIND. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE READ: B2's half (1) -- the OFF-LIMITS line -- is nearly REDUNDANT by construction, telling the model what LAST ACTION already told it for 15 more seconds. Half (2) -- the rejection naming the vetoed proposal with its args -- fires on every one of ~30 vetoes/bot-h and is the live treatment. The primary endpoint therefore tests half (2), and cooldown_did should be read as near-null BY DESIGN rather than as a failure of the change. This was not knowable from the tests, which all pass: it is a parameter interaction only the fleet could show.

amendments.what: the deciding field becomes vetoes_did_WARM (post-deploy minute 30 onward). Made BEFORE any deciding read.
amendments.why: The restart asymmetry I pre-registered as an 'activity dip' is far worse than that: it is a GATE STATE RESET, and it resets exactly the endpoint I chose. AdmissionControl's constructor clears BOTH `failedCooldowns` (admission.mjs:164) and `recent` (:165), and repeat_loop cannot fire until the bot has chosen 4 IDENTICAL ADMITTED actions (REPEAT_WINDOW = 4 at :22, tested at :701-703). So a restarted pool MECHANICALLY emits no repeat_loop vetoes for the first minutes and then emits excess cooldown vetoes as the map refills. That is precisely the +30 signature -- repeat_loop DiD -11.78, cooldown DiD +9.39 -- and it is a cleared gate, not a treatment effect. MEASURED CONFIRMATION: raw vetoes_did at +30 was -20.06; on the warm window it is -3.95. The raw number was ~80% warm-up. A third of that raw signal sat in learned_avoid (DiD -19.16), a class B2 does not touch at all, which was the tell. WHY WARM IS THE RIGHT FIELD AND NOT A CONVENIENT ONE: the null was measured with BOTH ARMS UNDISTURBED, so the estimator it calibrates is the uncontaminated one. Deciding the raw DiD against that null compares a restarted arm to a no-restart reference. The warm window makes the measurement match its calibration. The gate value is unchanged (-5.03) precisely because the null is unchanged. This is registered BEFORE the +90 and +180 reads and before any deciding number exists.
